parts.label: Understand
parts.title: Define the task population before collecting examples
parts.body:
An evaluation set should represent the work the system is being asked to do. Start with an inventory of task types, users, channels, languages, and consequences of error. Sample from actual work where permitted, with privacy safeguards, then add designed cases for rare severe failures that production frequency alone would underrepresent. Keep both views: a traffic-weighted measure for expected workload and a risk-focused measure for failures the organisation cannot average away.

Each case needs the input, relevant context, expected behaviour, source or policy version, risk label, and reason for inclusion. Some tasks have several acceptable answers. Write the essential constraints instead of one reference sentence that penalises a correct paraphrase. Have domain experts check whether cases sound like real requests and whether the expected answer is actually right.

Separate examples used to develop prompts from a held-out set used to assess release. If a team repeatedly studies failures in the held-out set and tunes to them, it has become a development set. Create fresh cases for a credible later assessment. Record when the data was collected and refresh it when policy, customer mix, or product changes.

example.title: Two views of support traffic
example.body: Routine order status makes up most support volume, while account-access errors are rarer and more harmful. The team reports overall traffic-weighted task success and a separate account-access safety gate. It does not hide the latter inside the former.

exercise.title: Build a case taxonomy
exercise.body: For a support assistant, define task categories, user groups, risk levels, and languages. Add at least two real-pattern cases and two designed severe cases per important slice. Document the source of expected behaviour and a privacy-safe handling method.

parts.label: Practice
parts.title: Audit coverage with a matrix
parts.body:
Make a matrix of task type by risk tier, then examine the case count in each cell. Add dimensions that matter in the workflow: language, region, document age, user entitlement, channel, and input quality. A single matrix cannot show every combination, so prioritise intersections that are common, consequential, or known to fail. Report empty and thin cells honestly.

A set of 100 clean order-status questions and two account-access cases may produce an attractive average while telling you little about access safety. Add restricted-account, revoked-access, and ambiguous-identity cases. Verify that the test data recreates the production permission path; a mock search index with no access control cannot test a release claim about confidentiality. For a bilingual service, measure each language rather than pooling them.

The coverage review is an executive tool. It tells leaders which tasks are supported by evidence and which remain excluded from launch. Ask whether the test distribution matches planned users and whether the severe cases exercise controls, not merely prompt phrasing.

example.title: A versioned coverage matrix
example.body: Set v1 has 240 held-out cases under policy corpus v4. Routine status has 120 English and 40 French cases (low impact); refunds have 30 English and 10 French (medium); account access has 30 English and 10 French (high). Ten account cases test revoked entitlement, but none combines French with revoked entitlement. The test mix is exactly two-thirds routine, one-sixth refund, and one-sixth account; expected traffic is 70%, 20%, and 10%. If 148/160 routine, 34/40 refund, and 30/40 account cases pass, overall success is 212/240 or 88.3%. Applying expected traffic weights to the three slice rates gives 70% × 92.5% + 20% × 85% + 10% × 75% = 89.25%. Report both, but neither average overrides a severe account-access gate. Before releasing French account access, add the missing intersection and verify policy version. All counts and shares are illustrative.

exercise.title: Find the blind spots
exercise.body: Create a task-by-risk matrix with case counts for a proposed assistant. Add region or language as a second view. Name three thin cells, why they matter, the cases needed, and whether the feature may launch without them.

sources: NIST AI RMF Core: context and measurement

parts.label: Operate
parts.title: Protect the meaning of a test result
parts.body:
Version the set, policy reference, system configuration, and grading rubric together. A policy answer can change from correct to wrong when the source changes. For cases with expert disagreement, record the dispute and resolve the expected outcome before using them as pass/fail gates. Remove leaked answers and duplicate cases that make the result appear more certain than it is. Check whether one template generated many near-identical items. Anthropic's agent evaluation guidance discusses task collection and grading; these local version and release rules make that evidence traceable to the business decision.

Use development, held-out, and production-sample pools for different purposes. Development cases guide iteration. Held-out cases support a release decision. Sampled production cases show whether real users and data still resemble either pool. Restrict access to sensitive cases, minimise personal data, and follow applicable local retention rules. Synthetic cases can test a boundary, but they should be reviewed for realistic wording and system state.

When an incident occurs, add a regression case that reproduces the failure, then examine nearby variants. A single memorised incident case proves only that one instance has been patched. Keep a record of why cases were added or retired so a changing score can be interpreted.

example.title: A policy version change
example.body: A leave-policy case expected a previous year's wording. HR updates the policy. The team versions the old case, creates a current one with the new expected behaviour, and reruns retrieval plus answer checks. It does not count the old answer as a model failure under the new policy.

exercise.title: Write a dataset change rule
exercise.body: Define who may add, revise, or retire a case; what evidence verifies its expected result; how to protect held-out cases; how to handle policy updates; and how an incident becomes a regression test.

parts.label: Apply
parts.title: State exactly what the dataset can support
parts.body:
A result is a claim about the tested tasks, configuration, and population. If the set covers English routine support for existing customers, it cannot establish readiness for French complaints, new customers, or payment actions. State exclusions and sample counts beside the score. For small samples, communicate uncertainty and use targeted testing before increasing exposure.

Bring a coverage map into the release meeting. Mark each capability as tested, thinly tested, or untested; add severity and the planned control. A thinly tested low-impact feature might launch with close human review. An untested write action should remain disabled. This makes scope a deliberate decision instead of an accidental consequence of a broad interface.

The CAIO should be able to connect each promised benefit and control to evidence. Where the evidence does not cover a claim, either gather the cases, narrow the product promise, or change the workflow so a person retains the decision.

example.title: An honest claim
example.body: 'On set v1's 160 routine-status cases (120 English, 40 French), 148 passed the agreed task check. Refund cases passed 34/40 and account-access cases 30/40. No test combines French with revoked account entitlement. Release is limited to read-only routine status for the tested users under policy corpus v4; refund and account actions remain with staff.' These are illustrative results from the same 240-case matrix, not evidence from a real service.

exercise.title: Write the scope statement
exercise.body: Using your case taxonomy, draft a four-sentence release claim that names supported tasks, population, counts, limitations, and excluded actions. Then write the next dataset collection step needed to broaden the claim.
